reading.body:
This record is a software reseller's office in Italy, not a data center, and should not appear in a map of AI infrastructure.

Factory Software operates as a regional sales and support office for AVEVA, a publicly traded industrial software company. AVEVA sells engineering design, operations management, and asset-performance software to manufacturing, energy, and process industries. The "Select" branding identifies this as part of AVEVA's network of reseller and systems-integrator partners. An office of this type maintains its own business IT systems but does not operate data-center infrastructure at scale.

The OpenStreetMap record that generated this entry was tagged as a telecom data center. This tagging appears to be an error. A software reseller's on-site server closet or IT infrastructure is not a data center in the sense relevant to AI compute capacity. The distinction matters because AI scaling depends on purpose-built facilities with dedicated power, cooling, and networking designed for high-density compute workloads. A partner office's IT closet serves business operations, not GPU clusters or the bulk compute that drives AI development.

This entry demonstrates a common risk in infrastructure mapping: legitimate infrastructure tags can be applied to non-infrastructure facilities, and company names alone do not establish what a location does. Cleaning this data requires checking what buildings actually house, not only what they are called or tagged.
